title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Premium Revision Paper #19

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the main job of leaves? (1 mark)
   A. Making food for the plant
   B. Making seeds
   C. Holding the plant in the soil
   D. Taking in water from the soil

2. The touch-me-not plant folds its leaves when touched. This shows that plants can (1 mark)
   A. respond to changes
   B. lay eggs
   C. eat food
   D. move from place to place

3. Which of these do animals breathe in from the air? (1 mark)
   A. Oxygen
   B. Water
   C. Smoke
   D. Dust

4. Which animal group breathes using gills? (1 mark)
   A. Reptiles
   B. Mammals
   C. Birds
   D. Fish

5. Which of these is a sign of life in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Being made of metal
   B. Being painted
   C. Staying in one place forever
   D. Feeding

6. Which part takes back most of the water from the leftover food? (1 mark)
   A. Large intestine
   B. Mouth
   C. Stomach
   D. Gullet

7. Which part of the digestive system is long and coiled? (1 mark)
   A. Rectum
   B. Small intestine
   C. Mouth
   D. Gullet

8. How often should teeth be brushed? (1 mark)
   A. Once a year
   B. Never
   C. Once a month
   D. At least twice a day

9. Which of these is NOT a part of the digestive system? (1 mark)
   A. Rectum
   B. Gullet
   C. Stomach
   D. Lungs

10. Why is diarrhoea dangerous for young children? (1 mark)
   A. They become taller
   B. They grow more teeth
   C. They lose water quickly
   D. They sleep too much

11. What does the rectum do? (1 mark)
   A. Makes saliva
   B. Digests proteins
   C. Stores faeces for a short time
   D. Chews food

12. What do teeth do in digestion? (1 mark)
   A. Digest food into the blood
   B. Cut and grind food into small pieces
   C. Take back water
   D. Store waste

13. In the mouth, which part helps to move food around and swallow? (1 mark)
   A. Gullet
   B. Rectum
   C. Tongue
   D. Stomach

14. Which of these is a reason we need gases? (1 mark)
   A. We can sit on them
   B. We can build houses with them
   C. We breathe air
   D. We can write with them

15. When reading a measuring jug, where should your eye be? (1 mark)
   A. Below the jug
   B. At the same level as the water surface
   C. Far from the jug
   D. Above the jug

16. Which of these gases do we breathe in to stay alive? (1 mark)
   A. Dust
   B. Petrol fumes
   C. Smoke
   D. Oxygen

17. Which of these breaks down and rots easily? (1 mark)
   A. Tin can
   B. Plastic bag
   C. Vegetable peelings
   D. Glass bottle

18. Which is an example of recycling? (1 mark)
   A. Buying less food
   B. Using a tin for a pencil holder
   C. Throwing paper in a bin
   D. Melting scrap metal to make new items

19. At a wedding, what can organisers do to keep the place clean? (1 mark)
   A. Throw waste in a river
   B. Burn plastic
   C. Provide bins and clean after the event
   D. Leave waste on the ground

20. Which disease can spread by mosquitoes breeding in old tins that hold water? (1 mark)
   A. Toothache
   B. Diarrhoea only
   C. Sunburn
   D. Malaria

21. What is a compost pit used for? (1 mark)
   A. Storing glass
   B. Turning kitchen waste into manure
   C. Storing plastic
   D. Burning waste

22. Which of these is e-waste? (1 mark)
   A. A paper bag
   B. A banana peel
   C. An old phone
   D. A leaf

23. Which of these is an example of reusing water? (1 mark)
   A. Buying bottled water
   B. Using water from washing vegetables to water plants
   C. Pouring water down the drain
   D. Leaving taps open

24. Why do we need water for farming? (1 mark)
   A. Crops and livestock need water
   B. To make wind
   C. To bake bricks only
   D. To make stones

25. When is the best time to water plants? (1 mark)
   A. Early morning or evening
   B. Midday only
   C. Never
   D. Noon

26. Why is saving water good for families? (1 mark)
   A. It stops rain
   B. It makes water heavier
   C. It reduces the water bill
   D. It causes floods

27. Which of these is a source of fresh water? (1 mark)
   A. A salty lake only
   B. A puddle of sea water
   C. A river
   D. The sea

28. Which of these is a way of increasing useful friction? (1 mark)
   A. Polishing a table
   B. Shoes with rough soles
   C. Oiling a floor
   D. Wearing smooth socks on a wet floor

29. Which surface gives the least friction? (1 mark)
   A. A wet, oiled tile
   B. A thick carpet
   C. Dry grass
   D. Rough sandpaper

30. A hockey stick hits a rolling ball to the left. What effect of force is this? (1 mark)
   A. Holds together
   B. Starts motion
   C. Changes direction
   D. Changes shape only

31. How can lights help protect a home? (1 mark)
   A. Lights make people sleep
   B. Lights make walls hot
   C. Lights make doors open
   D. Security lights help keep thieves away

32. Which of these is a natural source of light at night? (1 mark)
   A. A street lamp
   B. A candle
   C. Stars
   D. A torch

33. A flash of light in the sky during a storm is a natural source of light. What is it? (1 mark)
   A. A car headlight
   B. A lantern
   C. Lightning
   D. A solar lamp

34. Which of these is the biggest natural source of light for the Earth? (1 mark)
   A. The sun
   B. A star far away
   C. The moon
   D. A candle

35. Why should electric irons be unplugged after use? (1 mark)
   A. To make them heavier
   B. To make them hot
   C. To prevent burns and fire
   D. To make them noisy

36. Which instrument measures temperature? (1 mark)
   A. Thermometer
   B. Measuring jug
   C. Ruler
   D. Balance

37. Which of these is the biggest natural source of heat for the Earth? (1 mark)
   A. A fire
   B. An iron
   C. A kettle
   D. The sun

38. Why does hot tea cool down? (1 mark)
   A. It becomes heavier
   B. It gains light
   C. It gains cold
   D. It loses heat to the air and cup

39. What does a mother hen do for her chicks? (1 mark)
   A. Makes them wet
   B. Keeps them warm under her wings
   C. Feeds them iron
   D. Cools them

40. Which of these is a safety rule when cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Turn pot handles inwards
   B. Touch the hot pot
   C. Turn handles outwards
   D. Leave children alone at the cooker

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe how heat is used in cooking and warming in a home. (4 marks)

42. Describe an activity to observe the growth of a bean seed. Include what you need, what you do and what you record. (5 marks)

43. What should you do for a small burn? State three actions. (3 marks)

44. Describe the methods of conserving water. Include reducing, reusing and recycling with examples. (5 marks)

45. Explain why a kilogram of stones and a kilogram of feathers have the same mass but not the same volume. (4 marks)

46. Describe four effects of forces using examples from daily life. (4 marks)

47. Describe how you can care for plants at school and at home. Give five ways. (5 marks)

48. What is a force? Give one example of a push and one example of a pull. (2 marks)

49. Draw a table with two columns headed vertebrates and invertebrates. Place these animals correctly: goat, butterfly, snake, snail, hen, spider. (5 marks)

50. Name the parts of the digestive system in the order food passes through them. (2 marks)

51. Describe the natural and artificial sources of light and explain the difference. (5 marks)

52. Explain why a football is described as a container of matter although it looks empty. (3 marks)

53. Give two natural and two artificial sources of light. (2 marks)

54. Discuss how the three Rs can be used for waste from a school kitchen. (5 marks)

55. Explain the difference between reusing and recycling. (3 marks)

56. Describe how kitchen waste can be turned into manure. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Making food for the plant
   Leaves use sunlight, water and air to make food.

2. A — respond to changes
   Folding when touched is a response to a change in the surroundings.

3. A — Oxygen
   Animals need oxygen from the air or water.

4. D — Fish
   Fish take oxygen from water with gills.

5. D — Feeding
   Animals feed, grow, breathe, reproduce, remove waste, move, respond and die.

6. A — Large intestine
   The large intestine takes back water.

7. B — Small intestine
   The small intestine is a very long coiled tube.

8. D — At least twice a day
   Brushing morning and night keeps teeth healthy.

9. D — Lungs
   Lungs are for breathing.

10. C — They lose water quickly
   The body loses a lot of water and can become weak.

11. C — Stores faeces for a short time
   The rectum stores faeces before they pass out.

12. B — Cut and grind food into small pieces
   Chewing makes food smaller.

13. C — Tongue
   The tongue moves food and helps swallowing.

14. C — We breathe air
   Air gives us oxygen for breathing.

15. B — At the same level as the water surface
   This gives an accurate reading.

16. D — Oxygen
   Oxygen in the air is needed for life.

17. C — Vegetable peelings
   Vegetable peelings are decomposable.

18. D — Melting scrap metal to make new items
   Melting metal to make new items is recycling.

19. C — Provide bins and clean after the event
   Bins and cleaning keep the place tidy.

20. D — Malaria
   Mosquitoes spread malaria and breed in standing water.

21. B — Turning kitchen waste into manure
   Decomposable waste rots into compost.

22. C — An old phone
   E-waste means old electrical and electronic items.

23. B — Using water from washing vegetables to water plants
   Using water twice is reusing.

24. A — Crops and livestock need water
   Water is needed for plants and animals.

25. A — Early morning or evening
   Less water evaporates when it is cooler.

26. C — It reduces the water bill
   Less water used means less money paid.

27. C — A river
   Rivers carry fresh water that people can use.

28. B — Shoes with rough soles
   Rough soles grip the ground.

29. A — A wet, oiled tile
   Oil and smoothness reduce friction.

30. C — Changes direction
   The direction of the ball changes.

31. D — Security lights help keep thieves away
   Thieves avoid places where they can be seen.

32. C — Stars
   Stars give out their own light.

33. C — Lightning
   Lightning is a natural flash of light.

34. A — The sun
   The sun lights the Earth in the daytime.

35. C — To prevent burns and fire
   Switching off prevents accidents.

36. A — Thermometer
   A thermometer shows how hot something is.

37. D — The sun
   The sun heats the Earth.

38. D — It loses heat to the air and cup
   Heat goes from the tea to the cooler surroundings.

39. B — Keeps them warm under her wings
   Chicks need warmth.

40. A — Turn pot handles inwards
   Handles turned inwards cannot be knocked easily.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Heat from fire, gas or electricity cooks food making it soft and safer. Heat from fire or clothes keeps the body warm and chicks warm.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: You need a tin or container, soil, a bean seed and water. Plant the seed, water a little each day, measure the shoot with a ruler every two days and record heights in a table. Observe roots and leaves.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 mark for planting, 1 mark for watering, 1 mark for measuring, 1 mark for recording.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put it under cool running water, cover with a clean cloth, tell an adult and do not put butter or oil.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Reduce wastage: close taps. Reuse: washing vegetables water on plants. Recycle: cleaning used water at a treatment plant or filtering. Include rainwater harvesting.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three methods, 1 mark for correct examples and 1 mark for harvesting.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Both have 1 kg of matter. The feathers take up more space than the stones so their volume is larger.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for equal mass, 1 mark for the meaning of mass, 1 mark for feathers taking more space, 1 mark for volume being space.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: A force changes the shape of dough, starts a ball moving, stops a bicycle with brakes and changes the direction of a ball when hit with a stick.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each effect with an example.

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: Water when dry, weed, do not trample, plant trees, do not pick flowers, put waste in bins, protect from animals (any five).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way up to 5.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: A force is a push or a pull. A push: kicking a ball. A pull: opening a drawer.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for the two examples.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: Vertebrates: goat, snake, hen. Invertebrates: butterfly, snail, spider.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the table and 4 marks for placing the six animals (award 1 mark for two correct).

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, anus.
   Working / marking points: Award 2 marks for the correct order. 1 mark if at most two parts are out of order.

51. (5 marks)
   Answer: Natural sources are found in nature such as the sun, stars, lightning and fireflies. Artificial sources are made by people such as bulbs, torches and candles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for natural and artificial, 1 mark for examples of each and 1 mark for the difference.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is full of air. Air is a gas, so it has mass and takes up space. It keeps the ball in shape.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for air inside, 1 mark for air being matter, 1 mark for it filling the ball.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: Natural: sun, stars, lightning, firefly. Artificial: bulb, torch, candle, lantern, solar lamp.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct natural and 1 mark for two correct artificial.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: Reduce: cook and serve only what is needed. Reuse: use empty oil tins for storage and sacks for carrying. Recycle: sell scrap metal and paper, compost peelings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each R, 1 mark for one clear example and 1 mark for the compost point.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Reusing means using an item again in the same or a new way without changing it, for example a bottle for water. Recycling means turning waste into a new product, for example melting old plastic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reuse, 1 mark for recycle, 1 mark for one example.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put peelings and other kitchen waste with dry leaves and some soil in a compost pit. Decomposers rot it and after some weeks it turns to compost.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the pit, 1 mark for decomposers, 1 mark for compost.
